title: Countries and Cultures Around the World
summary: Fun facts about people, foods, festivals and greetings across the world.

steps.title: Different places, different ways
sentences: There are around two hundred countries in the world.
People in each country have their own languages, clothes, foods and festivals.
Learning about them helps us understand and respect each other.

steps.title: Greetings
sentences: In India we say namaste or vanakkam with folded hands.
In many countries people shake hands, and in New Zealand the Maori people greet by touching noses in a greeting called the hongi.

steps.title: Food and festivals
sentences: Rice is the main food for billions of people in Asia.
Italy is known for pasta, Mexico for tortillas and India for its many curries, idlis and dosas.
Festivals like Pongal, Diwali, Eid, Christmas and the Chinese New Year bring families together.

steps.title: What we share
sentences: Everywhere people love music, games, stories and their families.
Kindness is understood in every language.
The more we learn, the more we see how alike we are.

facts: Papua New Guinea has more than eight hundred languages, the most of any country.
Tamil is one of the oldest living languages in the world.
In Japan, taking off shoes before entering a home is the custom, just as in many Indian homes.

quiz.q: In Japan, what is a common greeting?
quiz.why: People often greet with a bow in Japan.

quiz.q: Which language is one of the oldest living languages?
quiz.why: Tamil has a very long recorded history and is still spoken today.
Understanding helps us live together kindly.
